html:
The Eighty Years' War, or Dutch Revolt, was the struggle of the Low Countries against the rule of Spain, from 1568 to 1648. It ended with the independence of the northern provinces as the Dutch Republic.

Under Philip II, heavy taxes, the persecution of Protestants and the brutal rule of the Duke of Alba drove nobles and towns to revolt, led by William the Silent. In 1579 the northern provinces joined in the Union of Utrecht, and in 1581 they declared Philip deposed. Spain reconquered the south, taking Antwerp in 1585.

During the war the Dutch built a trading empire and their Golden Age, and the East India Company was founded in 1602. Spain recognised Dutch independence at the Peace of Münster in 1648, part of the end of the Thirty Years' War. See the Netherlands.
